application.cv_markdown:
Tunde Tanaka

tunde.tanaka@mail.example | Oulu

EDUCATION

MSc Applied Physics, Politecnico del Naviglio, 2014

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Nordkom Radar Systems — Signal Processing Engineer
2015 – present

Based in Oulu since joining. Nordkom builds ground-based radar systems for weather and maritime surveillance.

Wrote and maintain the embedded signal processing firmware for Nordkom's current maritime radar: range compression, CFAR detection, and plot extraction in C on a TI C6678 multi-core DSP. Four channels processed simultaneously within a 500 µs PRI budget. I own the fixed-point implementation, cycle optimisation, and on-target debugging.

Built and maintain the production test framework in Python 3.10: approximately 6,000 lines controlling the RF test bench via SCPI, running automated acceptance tests, and generating per-unit reports. Used daily by the production team, version-controlled in GitLab, ~85% pytest coverage. Three other engineers contribute to the codebase.

Responsible for RF front-end calibration: R&S ZNB40 vector network analyser for S-parameter sweeps, noise-figure characterisation, and antenna pattern verification in the company's compact anechoic range.

Relocated to Oulu from Milan in 2015.

PROJECTS

Acoustic Beamforming for Hearing-Aid Microphone Arrays (Freelance, 2019–2021)
Designed and implemented a frequency-domain acoustic beamformer for a 4-microphone endfire array in a behind-the-ear hearing-aid prototype, contracted by a Danish audiology startup. Steered a cardioid beam toward the wearer's look direction using head-tracking IMU data, under constraints of <5 ms latency, <10 mW DSP budget, and a Cortex-M4F running at 64 MHz. Implemented in C, validated against measured data in a reverberant room. The startup used the prototype in their CE-marking clinical trial. Work performed under my Italian EU long-term residence permit (permesso di soggiorno di lungo periodo, granted 2019 after five continuous years of legal residence), which provides unconditional work authorisation across the EU. Registered with the Finnish Residency Records Agency upon relocating to Oulu.

Master's Thesis — Sparse DOA Estimation (Politecnico del Naviglio, 2014)
"Sparse Reconstruction Methods for Wideband Direction Finding." Developed compressive-sensing algorithms for direction-of-arrival estimation from wideband antenna arrays. The work drew directly on electromagnetic theory, statistical signal processing, and linear algebra from my applied physics degree. Conducted in English as part of PoliNaviglio's international MSc programme.

Published: T. Tanaka et al., "Sparse wideband DOA estimation via reweighted l1 minimisation," Proc. BALSIPCO, 2015.

SKILLS

- C (bare-metal, fixed-point DSP), Python (production tooling)
- RF measurement (VNA, spectrum analyser, anechoic range)
- MATLAB / Simulink
- Git, GitLab CI, TI Code Composer Studio, ARM Keil
- Linux, embedded RTOS
application.cover_letter_markdown:
To the hiring team at Kaikuvaara Oy,

Nordkom Radar Systems has been a good place to work for eleven years, and I'm not leaving because anything is wrong. The maritime radar product line has stabilised, I've maintained the firmware through three hardware revisions, and my scope for growth has reached a ceiling. I want to work somewhere the problems are harder.

My core deliverable at Nordkom is the embedded firmware for the maritime radar's signal processing chain. The current iteration runs on a TI C6678 and processes four receive channels within a 500 µs PRI: range compression via overlap-save FFT, CFAR detection with cell-averaging and ordered-statistic variants, and plot extraction — all in C, all fixed-point. I own the cycle budget and the on-target debugging. When something breaks on a customer installation, I'm the one who gets the call.

I also built and maintain the production test framework in Python — roughly 6,000 lines, 85% pytest coverage, used daily by the production team, CI via GitLab — and I'm responsible for RF front-end calibration: S-parameter sweeps on the R&S ZNB40 and pattern verification in the compact anechoic range. These tasks have become routine, which is honest about where I am and why I'm looking.

The most technically interesting project I've done outside Nordkom was a freelance contract designing an acoustic beamformer for a hearing-aid microphone array. The problem: steer a cardioid beam from a 4-element endfire array toward the wearer's look direction, fed by a head-tracking IMU, on a Cortex-M4F at 64 MHz with a <5 ms latency budget and <10 mW power ceiling. The application domain is nothing like radar, but the underlying work — spatial filtering, interference rejection, calibrating element-to-element gain and phase, making the algorithm fit on a constrained processor — was work I recognised. That project also convinced me I do my best work when the constraints are tight and the resources are small.

What I think I'd bring to Kaikuvaara: the embedded firmware discipline; the production Python tooling; the RF measurement experience; and — from the hearing-aid work — a demonstrated willingness to approach array-processing problems in unfamiliar domains and solve them. What I'd need to learn is the payload-specific context: mission constraints, environmental qualification, and the things that distinguish instrument-grade design from commercial radar. I'd rather state the gap plainly than have it surface after I've started.

On the practical side: I live in Oulu, have done since 2015, and I'm staying. I hold an EU long-term residence permit with unconditional work authorisation. All my professional work has been in English — Nordkom's working language — and my published conference paper (BALSIPCO 2015) and master's thesis from Politecnico del Naviglio are available on request.

I'm available for an interview whenever suits.

Tunde Tanaka

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
